Extract source-supported dates from the supplied raw paragraphs. Return only JSON matching the supplied schema, with a dates list covering every paragraph exactly once (groups of contiguous paragraphs are allowed). Preserve all original words; these are proposals, not human-approved history.
Use only dates explicitly evidenced in the supplied text or a supported forward continuation within the same region. Never carry a date backward from a later heading or across a region/chamber/proceeding boundary. Do not fill a missing date from catalog information or general historical knowledge. A month word used as an ordinary verb is not a date.
For each assignment include target_ids, value, date_kind, context_kind, status, method, evidence, alternatives, unknowns, basis. value is null for unknown, otherwise an object with start/end ISO strings, precision day/month/year and extent point/range. Evidence uses paragraph_id (the supplied alias), that paragraph's raw_sha256, exact quote, and half-open Unicode codepoint start/end offsets within the original raw_text. Copy the supplied hash exactly; do not compute or invent it. Offsets count original characters, including spaces.
A date present in the assigned target text uses date_kind explicit and method explicit_text; a supported forward continuation uses date_kind implicit and method scoped_continuation. Use context_kind proceeding or mentioned as supported and status proposed for dated proposals. Unknown dates use value null, date_kind none, context_kind unknown, status unknown, method no_supported_date, evidence [], alternatives [], a nonempty unknowns list and a short basis. Keep alternatives [] when no supported conflict is present; unknowns may be [] for a fully supported proposal. Never omit any paragraph or invent an alias, date, source reading, or human review status.

Use only supplied paragraph aliases. Keep dates within host-declared regions. Every paragraph needs a date proposal or explicit unknown; do not infer from catalog context.
